facts.raw_span: a 3-month history of brown-yellowish vaginal discharge
fluctuating lower abdominal pain
fever
progressive abdominal enlargement over 15 years, worsening in the last 5 years
difficulty with defecation and voiding
a smooth, firm pelvic mass was palpated extending to two fingers below the umbilicus, with limited mobility
the cervix could not be visualized or sondaged
elevated Cancer Antigen 125 level of 115.6 g/dL
a 269 × 529 mm hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity
a separate 126 × 106 mm homogeneous solid mass in the left adnexa with a clear border
a 145 × 110 × 146 mm multilocular cystic mass with thick septa and enhancing solid components
no lymphadenopathy was noted

concepts.why: The presence of a hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity and a separate solid mass in the left adnexa with a clear border, along with the patient's history of attempted myomectomy, supports this diagnosis.
The patient's symptoms of brown-yellowish vaginal discharge, fever, and the presence of a hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity, suggest an infected hematometra.
The presence of a separate solid mass in the left adnexa with a clear border, as seen on ultrasound and CT, is consistent with an ovarian fibroma.
The elevated Cancer Antigen 125 level and the presence of a multilocular cystic mass with thick septa and enhancing solid components, as seen on CT, raise the possibility of uterine adenocarcinoma.
The patient's symptoms of brown-yellowish vaginal discharge, fever, and pelvic pain, along with the presence of a smooth, firm pelvic mass, suggest pelvic inflammatory disease.

rationales.F01: Brown-yellowish vaginal discharge may indicate infection or malignancy, but is not specific enough to rule in or out any concept strongly.
rationales.F04: Progressive abdominal enlargement over 15 years is more likely to be associated with a slowly growing tumor such as leiomyoma or uterine adenocarcinoma.
rationales.F06: A smooth, firm pelvic mass is highly suggestive of a leiomyoma, especially given its size and limited mobility.
rationales.F09: The presence of a large hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity is highly suggestive of a leiomyoma with cystic degeneration or infected hematometra.
rationales.F10: A separate homogeneous solid mass in the left adnexa is highly suggestive of an ovarian fibroma.
rationales.F11: The multilocular cystic mass with thick septa and enhancing solid components is highly suggestive of a leiomyoma with cystic degeneration.

frontier_selector.rationale: The combination of a long history of progressive abdominal enlargement, the presence of a large hypoechoic mass within the uterine cavity, and a separate solid mass in the left adnexa with cystic degeneration supports the diagnosis of Leiomyoma with cystic degeneration, while the symptoms of brown-yellowish vaginal discharge and fever also suggest an infected component, hence Infected hematometra as a runner-up.
